messages:
jun: Heads-up — seeing an uptick in 5xx/retries from the /v1/infer clients. A bunch of traffic is landing on a couple of GPU nodes in us-west1-gpu-pool while others are almost idle.
ops-bot: ALERT: 10% pod retries on service redwood-infer-svc (app namespace) at 10:23 UTC.
elaine: which svc exactly? clusterIP or headless?
jun: clusterIP redwood-infer-svc in namespace app. kube-proxy is running in IPVS mode. ipvs stats look skewed, pasted small snippet below.
jun: ```
# ipvsadm -Ln --statistics
TCP  10.43.15.12:8080 rr
  -> 10.4.1.12:8080             Masq    1      0      8142        130ms
  -> 10.4.2.9:8080              Masq    1      0      211         6ms
  -> 10.4.3.7:8080              Masq    1      0      402         12ms
```
denver: That 8142 vs 211 looks like a hashing/sync problem rather than normal skew. Any conntrack drops?
liam: Seeing RDMA/eth errors on 10.4.2.9 around the same time in node logs: MTU mismatch on vxlan -> packet fragmentation. Might be causing retransmits and clients to retry.
jun: Also noticed kube-proxy versions vary across nodes (1.26.1 on some, 1.25.x on older nodes) — there was an ipvs sync bug backported in 1.26.2 that we may be hitting.
elaine: autoscaler didn't trigger because GPUs show as fully allocated on the hot nodes. That's inflating cost on a few nodes and increasing latency for others.
denver: Plan: restart kube-proxy on the 4 hottest nodes first (rolling) to force IPVS table resync. If that helps, schedule a controlled kube-proxy upgrade to 1.27 next week. I'll also cordon 10.4.2.9 and drain if RDMA issues persist.
liam: For debugging, I dumped conntrack counters and kernel logs, seeing conntrack entries spike and 'NETDEV WATCHDOG' on the same host. Snip: ```
# cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
24567
# dmesg | tail -n 5
[ 12345.678] NETDEV WATCHDOG: vxlan0: transmit queue 0 timed out
[ 12345.679] IPv4: martian source 10.43.15.1 from 10.4.2.9, dev vxlan0
```
jun: Temporary mitigation applied: moved 2 critical inference replicas to other nodes, and added a short TTL cache on client side to reduce retries. Observed partial rebalancing after kube-proxy restarts.
ops-bot: ACTION CREATED: SRE-7893 - investigate ipvs/hash sync + vxlan MTU; owner=denver; priority=high.
jun: After restart of kube-proxy on 10.4.1.12 and 10.4.3.7 traffic distribution normalized (see metrics). Still keeping 10.4.2.9 out of rotation for deeper kernel/RDMA investigation.
elaine: Good catch — cost spike was visible in last billing window because GPUs were saturated on few hosts. Schedule postmortem + cost mitigation playbook.
liam: Root cause summary candidate: mix of kube-proxy versions causing IPVS table inconsistencies + an MTU/RDMA issue on one node that amplified retries. Recommend cluster-wide kube-proxy version sync, kernel patch for vxlan MTU, and a quick gating check in autoscaler to add capacity when per-node GPU saturation exceeds 80%.
denver: I'll own the kube-proxy rollout and the ticket. Will post updates in SRE board. :thumbsup:
elaine: thanks — please post remediation steps + rollback plan in SRE-7893.
sre-oncall: assigning oncall for monitoring checks for the next 48h.
